newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ AND VISA TRIAL INTERNET TRANSACTIONS.
newsitem.headline: ANZ AND VISA TRIAL INTERNET TRANSACTIONS.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and Visa International announced on Thursday a joint programme to trial secure electronic transactions across the Internet.
The trial, to start later this year, would allow Australian Visa card holders to buy goods and services over the internet "confidently and securely", ANZ said.
ANZ's chief general manager cards division, Charles Carbonaro, said the trial was the first for an Australian bank.

"Both customers and merchants have been expressing a desire for ANZ to offer this type of service, but to date the security aspects associated with electronic commerce have been a deterrent," he said in statement.
The trial would involve ANZ Visa cardholders and merchants using digital certificate software which provides electronic identification and confidentiality across the Internet.
"The software uses state-of-the-art encryption technology, designed to scramble electronic messages, ensuring they cannot be read or tampered with as they cross the Internet," ANZ said.
The bank said it would use 'electronic keys' to decrypt these messages and authenticate instructions from cardholders and merchants.
